rationale: Measured facts: the timed unit is GPU-bound. execution_timeline-1221e205 shows 88 kernels with kernel_active_union_us=4097.5 of kernel_span_us=4176.8 (gaps 79.2us) inside a 4.466ms workload window, and python_runtime-aea48e29 shows host time dominated by cuda_synchronize (2.07ms of ~2.15ms cumulative in _infer) with all dispatch (torch.conv2d 0.43ms, torch.batch_norm 0.33ms, torch.relu 0.13ms) hidden under GPU execution; the clean original baseline is latency_ms 4.251697. So latency must come down by removing/fusing GPU kernel work, not host dispatch. The dominant non-conv GPU work sits in the transformers ResNetConvLayer modules (conv2d -> BatchNorm2d -> ReLU/Identity): aten::batch_norm costs 428.0us and aten::relu 343.9us of the 4168.5us diagnostic CUDA total. The five selected groups are the complete ResNetConvLayer family (17 module calls covering the stem 7x7 conv layer and both conv positions of all 8 ResNetBasicLayers, inclusive 3645.5us = 87.4% of the project call; conv shapes 64x3x7x7 s2, 64/128/256/512x3x3 and their stride-2 variants, verified per call in calls.json). Their structure is uniform: eval-mode BatchNorm2d with frozen running stats followed by ReLU on 9 of 17 sites (conv2 sites use Identity, verified in the installed transformers 5.16.1 source). Optimization: replace each ResNetConvLayer forward with an equivalent that folds its eval BatchNorm exactly into the conv (W' = W * gamma/sqrt(var+eps) per output channel, b' = beta - gamma*mu/sqrt(var+eps)) and evaluates conv+bias(+ReLU where present) as one fused cudnn call, e.g. torch.ops.aten.cudnn_convolution_relu(self, W', b', stride, padding, dilation, groups) available in the worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129, with a per-site fallback to aten.conv2d(W', b') + aten.relu if the fused engine declines a shape. This is a module-boundary replacement (direct callable per binding-contract, no global functional dispatch); the 3 ResNetShortCut conv+BN pairs, residual adds, MaxPool2d, AdaptiveAvgPool2d and classifier are outside this boundary and stay untouched. All frozen FP32 policies are preserved: dtype float32, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn (the fused op reads the global cudnn context flags), cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', inference_mode; weights remain the pinned pretrained revision, only algebraically transformed per-module in eval. Removed GPU work is 17 batch_norm kernels (401.4us; the other 26.5us are the 3 shortcut BNs left intact) and 9 relu kernels (280.2us; the 8 post-add basic-layer ReLUs, 63.7us, are outside the family and remain): 681.6us of inclusive diagnostic CUDA time, ~16.4%, dropping kernel count from 88 toward ~62. Constraint images_per_second >= 0.95 x baseline is the exact reciprocal of latency_ms on the same batch-32 workload, so it holds for any genuine improvement.
hypothesis: Folding eval-mode BatchNorm into the conv weights and evaluating conv+bias+ReLU as a single fused FP32 cudnn op inside all 17 ResNetConvLayer modules reduces GPU busy time by roughly the removed elementwise kernel time (681.6us diagnostic-inclusive, ~16%), which, because the invocation is GPU-bound (>=92% kernel-busy window, host waits in cuda_synchronize), translates close to linearly into the clean wall metric: expect latency_ms from 4.2517 toward ~3.5-3.65ms (roughly 14-17% improvement) with images_per_second rising correspondingly above the 0.95 floor. Numerics: BN folding is exact in real arithmetic and only reassociates FP32 rounding (order 1e-7 relative), and fused ReLU is the same elementwise max, so full 32x1000 logits should stay well inside atol=rtol=1e-4 with identical top-1 and the +1-corruption control still rejected; the repeated-forward closeness check in observe() must also pass with the same folded implementation on both runs. Risks to test: (1) whether cudnn 9.20 services conv+bias+relu fusion for every shape at FP32 with TF32 disabled - per-site fallback keeps at least the 401us BN-kernel removal; (2) whether the fused conv kernel for some shape (notably the 7x7 stride-2 stem on 32x3x224x224) is slower than the unfused scudnn kernel, shrinking the stem's 444us elementwise gain; (3) the observe() repeat forward must use the same replacement so its comparison stays apples-to-apples. The benefit estimate is a hypothesis from diagnostic CUDA durations, not a measured clean-timing result; the framework's independent measurement decides acceptance.
